newsitem.title: MEXICO: Construction slump in W. Mexico continues - industry.
newsitem.headline: Construction slump in W. Mexico continues - industry.

text.p: Construction industry output in the powerful western Mexican state of Jalisco is lagging behind 1995 levels, an industry leader said on Wednesday.

"First-half production this year was 708 million pesos, so we will close 1996 with 1.4 billion pesos, or maybe 1.5 billion pesos," said Jose Luis Macias, Jalisco delegate to the National Construction Industry Chamber.
Construction output totalled 1.679 billion pesos in Jalisco in 1995, itself well down on the 1994 total of 2.837 billion pesos. Jalisco is home to Mexico's second biggest city of Guadalajara.
Nationwide construction output figures for full year 1995 and first-half 1996 were 35.375 billion pesos and 18.708 billion pesos, respectively.
In other parts of Mexico, the construction industry has begun to rebound, mostly fueled by public spending infrastructure projects.
